requirements.requirement: Documented JSON conversion rules shared with input variables
requirements.details: Parse JSON and JSON dataset files reuse the input-variable converter: i32 Int tokens, f32 decimal/exponent tokens rounded directly, null to None, last duplicate key, one leading BOM ignored, 128 nested containers.
Catchable BW3003 messages name JSON paths or serde line/column, CSV line/column or record widths, and header problems; dataset files fail discovery with BW7002 located in the data file.
Parse CSV and From CSV datasets read header-row RFC 4180 tables with LF/CRLF records, doubled quotes, BOMs, and String fields.
Nested JSON is ordinary collection data; missing keys fail with BW3004 path/segment details. Canonical JSON round-trips nested values with identical kinds.
Covers i32 bounds, f32 max/min-positive/subnormal/underflow/negative zero/rounding, escapes, surrogate pairs, lone surrogates, non-ASCII keys and fields, and BOMs.

Example 39 reads JSON dataset rows, fetches each user document from a loopback fixture, parses the body, and asserts nested fields; a changed row fails only itself with dataset/row identity, and a missing resource reports the status mismatch.
Each converted node grows the temporary reservation before allocation; CSV results are measured before the building pass; value/temporary limits raise BW8001.

documentation_updates.change: Mark the verified structured-data roadmap entry complete.

validation_scope: Full GNU/musl debug/release suites: 1,774 tests each; strict Clippy for both targets, formatting, coverage/mutation helper checks. 16 focused structured-data mutations use library/CLI unit, structured-data, and allocation tests in an isolated source snapshot. No new generated campaign score is claimed.
review_notes: The JSON converter gained an admission hook instead of a second implementation, so Parse JSON, JSON dataset files, and CLI input variables share one conversion rule set, including exact decimal-to-f32 parsing from raw token text. A unit test proves the per-node growth totals equal the converted value's accounted size, including duplicate keys whose discarded values are never admitted.

The fixed catalogue grew from 97 to 100 signatures. Count assertions, snapshot-entry thresholds (shifted by exactly three), the CLI listing, two library doctests, and ten documentation statements were updated; the snapshot capacity bound (178) still holds.
The dataset format keyword initially matched a trailing space because pest inserts implicit whitespace between tokens in non-atomic rules; the rule is now atomic.
The dataset loader callback now receives the declared format, and the discovery cache keys parses by (canonical path, format). A test declares one file in two formats to prove separate parsing.

The JSON string escaper moved from assertion diagnostics into the structured-data module and now uses short escapes for common controls; assertion typed operands remain valid JSON and their documented guarantees are unchanged.
The loopback HTTP fixture gained a directory-serving mode that mirrors the documented python3 -m http.server command; the fixed-body mode is unchanged.
limits: Parse JSON retains the input-variable duplicate-key rule (last value wins) for consistency; duplicates are not rejected.
Canonical JSON is deterministic and round-trips Botwork values but is not RFC 8785 JCS: numbers use shortest f32 text and keys sort by Unicode scalar value.
CSV support is comma-delimited with a required header row; other delimiters, headerless tables, and type inference are not provided. Fields are Strings and convert explicitly.
Container backing storage for arrays and maps is allocated after the per-container entry checks but is not itself charged as payload, matching the existing value-accounting model.
JSON and CSV dataset rows have no tags; their names equal their IDs. Dataset conversion errors inside a row report the file and JSON path without a source range.
HTTP response bodies are not parsed automatically; Parse JSON is explicit.

from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import subprocess, json, hashlib, re, tempfile, os
root=Path.cwd()
out=Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="structured-validation-",dir=root/"target"))
print(f"validation record: {out / 'summary.json'}",flush=True)
def measured():
 inputs=[p for d in ('src','tests','examples') for p in (root/d).rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in p.parts]
 inputs += sorted((root/'docs').rglob('*.md')) + [root/'README.md']
 inputs += [root/p for p in ('Cargo.toml','Cargo.lock','.cargo/mutants.toml','scripts/coverage.py','scripts/mutation_core.py')]
 return {str(p.relative_to(root)):hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in sorted(inputs)}
musl_cc=str(root/'target/http-musl-toolchain/root/usr/bin/musl-gcc')
record={'complete':False,'started':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'revision':subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip(),'input_sha256':measured(),'musl_compiler':musl_cc,'checks':[]}
musl=['--target','x86_64-unknown-linux-musl']
commands=[('gnu-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked']),('gnu-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release']),('musl-debug-full',['cargo','test','--locked',*musl]),('musl-release-full',['cargo','test','--locked','--release',*musl]),('clippy-gnu',['cargo','clippy','--locked','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('clippy-musl',['cargo','clippy','--locked',*musl,'--all-targets','--','-D','warnings']),('format',['cargo','fmt','--all','--','--check']),('coverage-helper',['python3','tests/coverage_tools.py']),('mutation-helper',['python3','tests/mutation_tools.py'])]
try:
 for label,command in commands:
  print('running '+label,flush=True)
  log=out/(label+'.log')
  with log.open('w') as stream:
   result=subprocess.run(command,stdout=stream,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,timeout=2400,env=dict(os.environ,CARGO_BUILD_JOBS='4',CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_musl=musl_cc))
  content=log.read_text()
  rows=re.findall(r'test result: (?:ok|FAILED)\. (\d+) passed; (\d+) failed; (\d+) ignored;',content)
  check={'label':label,'command':command,'status':result.returncode,'log':str(log.relative_to(root)),'tests':dict(zip(('passed','failed','ignored'),[sum(int(row[i]) for row in rows) for i in range(3)])),'log_sha256':hashlib.sha256(log.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
  record['checks'].append(check)
  (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
  print(json.dumps(check),flush=True)
  if result.returncode:
   print(content[-12000:],flush=True)
   raise SystemExit(result.returncode)
 record['inputs_unchanged']=measured()==record['input_sha256']
 record['complete']=record['inputs_unchanged']
finally:
 record['finished']=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
 (out/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(record,indent=2)+'\n')
print('complete' if record['complete'] else 'INPUTS CHANGED', flush=True)

"""Run the documented example-39 workflow with the release binary and Python's http.server."""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json, socket, subprocess, sys, time
root = Path("/home/dhilipsiva/projects/dhilipsiva/botwork")
binary = root / "target/release/botwork"
out = Path(sys.argv[1])
with socket.socket() as probe:
    probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    port = probe.getsockname()[1]
server = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "http.server", str(port), "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--directory", "examples/fixtures/users"],
                          cwd=root, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
checks = []
try:
    for _ in range(100):
        try:
            socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=0.2).close()
            break
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.05)
    result = subprocess.run([binary, "--suite", "examples/39-dataset-http.suite.botwork", "--jobs", "2", "--var", f'base_url="http://127.0.0.1:{port}"'],
                            cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    checks.append({"check": "documented Python fixture workflow for example 39", "status": result.returncode,
                   "summary": result.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1] if result.stderr.strip() else "",
                   "both_rows_succeeded": "[cases] 2 selected: 2 succeeded, 0 failed" in result.stderr})
finally:
    server.terminate()
    server.wait(timeout=10)
doc = (root / "docs/structured-data.md").read_text()
source = doc.split("<!-- botwork-test: structured-data -->\n```botwork\n", 1)[1].split("```", 1)[0]
(out / "structured-doc.botwork").write_text(source)
result = subprocess.run([binary, "--file", str(out / "structured-doc.botwork")], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
checks.append({"check": "documented example", "status": result.returncode,
               "stdout_matches": result.stdout == (root / "tests/doc-examples/structured-data.stdout").read_text()})
summary = {"binary_sha256": hashlib.sha256(binary.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), "checks": checks}
(out / "manual.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
